Question: The average (arithmetic mean) of \(10\) different positive whole numbers is \(10.\) The largest possible value of any of these numbers is
Solution:
The mean fixes the total of the ten numbers:
\[
10\times10=100.
\]
To make one number as large as possible, make the other nine numbers as small as their conditions allow. Since they are different positive whole numbers, their smallest possible values are \(1,2,\ldots,9\), whose sum is \(45\). Therefore the remaining number is at most
\[
100-45=55.
\]
This bound is attained by \(1,2,\ldots,9,55\). These ten numbers are distinct and positive, and their sum is \(100\), so their mean is \(10\). The largest possible value is \(\boxed{55}\), choice \(\boxed{\text{C}}\).
